# Hello!

![](cowboy_hat_edited.png){style="border-radius: 50%; object-fit: cover; object-position: center 30%" width="200"}
:::

My name is Jared Vasil ([CV](papers/cv_sept26.pdf), [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=h2CNbSMAAAAJ&hl=en)). I am a psychologist interested in how people think about themselves ("self-conception"). To study this topic, I investigate the communicative and social behavior of children and great apes.

Currently, I am a Postdoctoral Fellow at the [Center for Possible Minds](https://www.possibleminds.org/) and in the [COMPARE Lab](https://www.comparelab.org/) at Indiana University. I earned my PhD from Duke University in 2024 under the supervision of Michael Tomasello.

My peer-reviewed journal articles with their associated data and code are below.

**keywords**: development; evolution; self-conception; communication; collaboration; Bayes

# Peer-Reviewed Journal Articles

PDFs of either the published article or the accepted manuscript are hyperlinked. Asterisks indicate mentees. These individuals contributed substantively to study conceptualization, design, data collection, and analysis en route to a thesis.

*Instructions*: Data and code are hyperlinked below their associated publication. Clicking the hyperlink will download a .zip file. Inside of this .zip file is a folder system with a .Rproj file. The published analysis can be reproduced by running the .r or .rmd script within the .Rproj file. The folder system is configured so that the entire analysis pipeline - from data import to posterior inference, including figures and tables - can be completed in one command (plus commands for package installation, if any).

I principally use tools from [tidyverse](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tidyverse/index.html) for data manipulation, [brms](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/brms/index.html) for modeling, [posterior](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/posterior/index.html) for posterior analysis, and [tidybayes](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tidybayes/index.html) for visualization.
